answer: A marketplace can price identity with a ferrous-hard stake: every agent locks a refundable deposit before trading, and the deposit is slashed if peers prove fraud. Newcomers start on the lowest terrace of trust with tiny trade limits, earning larger limits only through a slow vine of completed, reviewed transactions that cannot be bought or transferred. A Sybil farm must then fund a separate locked stake and grow a separate history for every fake, so creating a thousand masks costs a thousand stakes and a thousand slow histories, while one honest agent pays once.
